cards.headline: St. Lucie Precincts 39 and 52 Get New Polling Site for Nov. 3 Election
cards.teaser: Voters in two St. Lucie County precincts will cast ballots at a new location after renovations closed their usual polling place. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker is also urging residents to use early voting to avoid Election Day lines.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County voters assigned to Precincts 39 and 52 will vote at a temporary polling place for the Nov. 3 general election because of renovations at their usual site. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker announced Tuesday that voters in the two precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce.

Walker encouraged voters to take advantage of early voting, including at the county's newest early voting site, Lakewood Park Branch Library, 7605 Santa Barbara Drive in Fort Pierce, to avoid lines on Election Day. Early voting hours run until 6 p.m. at locations across the county, including the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the Zora Neale Hurston Library at 3008 Avenue D in Fort Pierce, the MIDFlorida Credit Union Event Center at 9221 SE Event Center Place in Port St. Lucie, the Community Center at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Lewis Library at 2950 Rosser Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence at 500 NW California Blvd. in Port St. Lucie and Minsky Gym at 750 SW Darwin Blvd. in Port St. Lucie.

Voters who want to cast a ballot by mail must request one by the deadline set by the Supervisor of Elections office. Walker's office is encouraging anyone returning a ballot by mail to do so at least seven days before Election Day to ensure it arrives in time to be counted.

Vote-by-mail ballots can also be dropped off in person at any early voting site or at designated Supervisor of Elections locations, including the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the St. Lucie West South County Annex at 250 NW Country Club Drive in Port St. Lucie, the Conrad Administration Annex at 1664 SE Walton Road in Port St. Lucie and the Tradition Tax Collector office at 10264 SW Village Parkway in Port St. Lucie. Voters with questions about their assigned precinct or the location changes can contact the Supervisor of Elections office ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

hero.headline: Sheriff Flowers Investigates If Teen's Fatal Shooting at Garcia's Boat Ramp Was Self-Defense
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators are examining whether the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp was an act of self-defense. The shooting happened during a confrontation at the waterfront spot, which authorities say has become a popular meetup location for teenagers.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the 17-year-old open the door of a truck and throw punches at people inside before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said during a news conference. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video of the confrontation moments before the shooting.

Both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and vehicle involved, according to authorities. As of Monday, no arrests had been made. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," Flowers said. The investigation remains active, and the sheriff is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

Flowers said social media has played a role in drawing large groups of teenagers to locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp and warned that the presence of firearms is raising the risks tied to those gatherings. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." Flowers also urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as one way to help keep them safe.

hero.headline: Fellsmere Teen Meetup Shooting Leaves Sebastian River Student Dead, Sheriff Cites Self-Defense Claim
hero.teaser: Sulliman Bah, 17, died after a gathering of more than 100 teens at Garcia's Boat Ramp turned violent. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers says a self-defense claim may apply.
hero.body:
A 17-year-old has been identified as the teen killed in a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Fellsmere, where a meetup of more than 100 teens turned violent. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the gathering included teens ages 14 to 19, with drinking and fighting reported before the shooting around 11:24 p.m. The family confirmed the victim was Sulliman Bah, a senior at Sebastian River High School who had recently withdrawn from the school to be home schooled, according to a district spokesperson.

According to detectives, Bah and a group of friends approached a pickup truck occupied by two 18-year-olds. Bah opened the truck door and attempted to punch someone inside when the passenger fired a single shot, striking him. Friends carried Bah toward Fellsmere, where deputies and EMS met them at Fellsmere City Hall and performed CPR. He was taken first to Sebastian River Medical Center, then transported to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries.

No arrests have been made. Flowers said the driver and passenger from the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the truck and the firearm used in the shooting. Investigators used Flock technology to identify people connected to the vehicle and the shooting, and deputies recovered additional guns and multiple shell casings at the scene. The sheriff said the preliminary investigation points toward a self-defense claim. "We will be submitting a warrant in the case, but at this time it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim as a result," Flowers said, adding that the State Attorney's Office will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. Flowers said there may have been as many as four fights at the boat ramp that night and that the group involved had "a history of fighting," calling it "an ongoing thing."

Flowers said the meetup reflects a growing trend of teens gathering at remote locations arranged through Snapchat, where fights are recorded and shared online. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," he said. "We've got kids out here losing their lives trying to go viral on social media." He warned that combining guns with teen gatherings is dangerous, saying, "It's not safe. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead." Flowers urged parents to ask their children whether they attended the meetup and asked anyone who witnessed or recorded the shooting to contact investigators. The School District of Indian River County said it is "heartbroken" by Bah's death and had grief counselors available over the weekend, including at Sebastian River High School's Homecoming Dance, with support continuing as students and staff returned to school.

cards.teaser: The Florida Highway Patrol says a 53-year-old Fort Pierce man died when his box truck slammed into the back of another truck on A1A at Regatta Drive. The crash shut down the intersection in Vero Beach.
cards.body:
The Florida Highway Patrol says the driver killed in Monday's crash that closed State Road A1A at Regatta Drive in Vero Beach was a 53-year-old man from Fort Pierce. FHP says he was driving an Isuzu box truck south on A1A behind a Freightliner roll-off truck operated by a 25-year-old Fort Pierce man.

The roll-off truck was slowing for traffic ahead when the box truck failed to slow in time, FHP said. The front of the box truck struck the rear of the roll-off truck.

Indian River County Fire Rescue personnel pronounced the box truck driver dead at the scene at 4:46 p.m. from injuries suffered in the collision.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Woman Pleads Guilty in Palm Beach County Apartment Theft Scheme
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman pleaded guilty Monday to stealing tens of thousands of dollars from residents of a Palm Beach County apartment complex while working as their community manager. Ashley R. Clayton, 38, entered a guilty plea on Oct. 5 to money laundering, organized scheme to defraud and making false entry in book of business entity, according to Palm Beach County court documents. Clayton agreed to the plea deal on Sept. 28.

Clayton was sentenced to five years of probation on each charge, to be served concurrently. She was credited with 12 days already served in Palm Beach County jail and ordered to pay court costs and complete community service. She must also undergo mental health and substance abuse evaluations and is banned from handling any financial transactions for a business or another person. Under the plea agreement, Clayton and the victim will work out how much restitution she owes the property management company.

According to a Riviera Beach Police Department report, Clayton worked for three months as community manager at Berkeley Landing Apartments, located at 3100 Broadway, where she oversaw rent payments, deposits, application fees, background and credit checks, and the compliance application process. A regional manager for the complex told police on June 13, 2024, that Clayton had been directing residents to pay through Zelle, with the money going into her personal bank account. Some residents gave her blank money orders. Police said Clayton sent residents a letter on apartment complex letterhead telling them rent had to be paid by money order "until further notice" while payment ledgers were being updated, a letter the complex never authorized her to send.

After she was fired, Clayton returned to the property and handed over 20 money orders worth $14,798.22 to management, but police said she kept three others and tried to cash them at an Amscot in Miami. One was successfully cashed, leaving the complex short at least $11,999.23. Investigators determined Clayton collected $31,249.32 through Zelle transfers, bringing the total stolen to at least $58,046.77. The police report identified five additional people from whom Clayton took money under false pretenses while employed at the complex.

hero.headline: Mother of Teen Killed at Indian River Boat Ramp Disputes Self-Defense Claim
hero.body:
The mother of the 17-year-old boy killed during a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County is disputing claims that the shooting was self-defense. Sulliman Bah died after being shot by a passenger in a white pickup truck during a party that drew about 1,000 teenagers to the boat ramp, just south of Fellsmere. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said Monday that investigators are examining whether the shooting was justified, but Bah's mother says her son was trying to protect others, not attack anyone.

At a news conference Monday afternoon, Flowers showed two videos of the shooting from different angles. The footage begins with Bah approaching the truck. "Seventeen-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. One shot is fired," Flowers said. The sheriff said the shot came from the passenger seat and killed Bah. Flowers said Bah had a history with the two 18-year-olds inside the truck, including prior fights, and that the pair told investigators they had the gun for protection. "At this time, it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim," Flowers said.

Bah's mother rejects that account. In a text message to a reporter, she said, "Sulliman was a defender of his friends. Always protecting the underdog, and I believe he was trying to save the crowd from that gun that he knew was about to be used...He was there to protect his friends from the thugs that had previously threatened him and many others multiple times." She said she does not see her son throwing a punch in the video. "If anything, I believe he was attempting to push the gun away," she said.

The sheriff's office has not released the identities of the two 18-year-olds in the truck, but Flowers said they are cooperating with investigators. No arrests have been made. Flowers said prosecutors will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. "It's going to be up to the state on whether charges ultimately will be filed. But I can tell you self-defense plays a part in these," he said. The sheriff said the investigation remains active and asked anyone who attended the party at Garcia's Boat Ramp to contact his office.

hero.headline: IRC Sheriff: Video Shows Teen Punching Before Fatal Boat Ramp Shooting
hero.body:
A 17-year-old died in a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, and the sheriff said Monday that investigators are examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense. Sheriff Eric Flowers held a news conference Monday to release new details, including video evidence, in a case that remains under investigation with no arrests made.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the 17-year-old opening the door of a truck and throwing punches at people inside just before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video of the confrontation that occurred moments before the shooting.

Authorities said both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident. Flowers said it will ultimately be up to the State Attorney's Office to decide whether charges are filed. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," he said.

Flowers said the shooting happened during a confrontation at Garcia's Boat Ramp, which has become a popular meetup spot for large groups of teenagers, often organized through social media. He warned that the combination of social media and firearms is making those gatherings more dangerous. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." He urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as a way to help keep them safe. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

cards.headline: New $100M I-95 Interchange at Oslo Road Opens in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis joined state transportation officials Monday to open the new Oslo Road interchange, the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis was in Indian River County on Monday to celebrate the completion of a new $100 million I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, a project state officials say will improve traffic flow, emergency response times and freight movement. The interchange opened about a year ahead of schedule and marks the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.

DeSantis said the project provides a new direct connection to I-95 while easing congestion at nearby interchanges at Indrio Road and State Road 60. "This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit," DeSantis said. According to the governor, drivers using Oslo Road to access I-95 can expect travel times to be cut roughly in half. State transportation officials project traffic along the corridor will continue growing through 2045.

DeSantis said the project is also expected to bring significant public safety benefits. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could be reduced by as much as 56%, allowing first responders to reach crashes and other emergencies more quickly. "This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations," DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said improved access to I-95 for first responders was one of the project's most important features. "Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. The new interchange is also expected to improve freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County by giving trucks and commercial traffic a more direct route to the interstate.

State officials said the project was accelerated through Florida's Moving Florida Forward initiative, a transportation funding program launched by the DeSantis administration to speed up major road projects across the state. Perdue said FDOT worked with contractors through a "voluntary acceleration" program that rewarded construction teams for finishing projects more quickly, which helped the Oslo Road interchange finish about 400 days ahead of schedule. FDOT also acquired land near the interchange to establish a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which state officials said will serve as the only relocation area of its kind in Southeast Florida, allowing protected tortoises to be moved while infrastructure projects continue. The Oslo Road interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across Florida's Treasure Coast region. "This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future," DeSantis said.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Police Arrest Two in South 6th Street Shooting
hero.body:
Fort Pierce Police have arrested two 18-year-olds in connection with a shooting that erupted from a domestic dispute on South 6th Street over the weekend. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of attempted first-degree homicide, and Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact. Both were arrested on Saturday, Oct. 3, the Fort Pierce Police Department announced Monday.

According to a police statement, officers responded to the 600 block of South 6th Street at 7:12 a.m. on Oct. 3 after the victim called 911 and said someone had pulled a gun and started shooting at her. Police said the victim had gone to the location to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. Several people then came out of the residence and attacked her, according to police.

The victim managed to escape the attack and get into her vehicle to drive away, police said. As she drove off, Lopez-Godoy retrieved a rifle from the property and fired shots toward her vehicle, according to the police statement. hero.headline: Winter Haven Bus Crash Death Revives Seatbelt Fight Rooted in St. Lucie County
hero.body:
A fatal school bus crash in Polk County is reigniting scrutiny of Florida's weak seatbelt requirements, 14 years after a St. Lucie County bus crash first prompted federal investigators to urge the state to mandate stronger restraints. A 10th grader headed to Winter Haven High School was killed Monday morning when a school bus carrying 39 people crashed. Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd called it heartbreaking at a morning news briefing, saying the district lost "one fatality of a beautiful high school girl." Investigators have not released how many students were wearing seatbelts, what type of restraints were on the bus, or whether the belts affected the outcome of the crash.

Florida law requires school buses built since 2001 to have seatbelts, but it does not require students to wear them and does not require the lap-and-shoulder belts that federal safety investigators consider far more protective. Most Florida school buses, including every bus in the Polk County school district according to a district spokesperson, are equipped only with standard lap belts.

The gap between Florida law and federal recommendations traces back to a 2012 crash in St. Lucie County, where a school bus collided with a semi-truck and killed 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp. Aaron was wearing the bus's standard lap belt when he died. The National Transportation Safety Board later investigated the crash and tested how different seatbelt designs affect student safety. Its simulations found that lap-and-shoulder belts control a passenger's movement far better in a crash than lap belts alone, leading the agency to recommend that all school buses nationwide, and specifically all new large school buses in Florida, be equipped with lap-and-shoulder restraints. Florida never adopted that recommendation into law.

Nearly 15 years after Aaron Beauchamp's death, about 20% of St. Lucie County school buses still use only lap belts rather than the safer lap-and-shoulder restraints. Transportation safety experts note that deadly school bus crashes are extremely rare and that buses remain the safest way for students to travel to and from school, but Monday's crash is likely to renew pressure on state lawmakers to revisit Florida's seatbelt standards. Polk County Schools Superintendent Fred Heid said after the crash, "No one will ever understand how heavy this weighs on our hearts."

hero.headline: Family Identifies Teen Killed at Indian River County Boat Ramp, No Arrests Yet
hero.body:
The family of a 17-year-old killed in a shooting at an Indian River County boat ramp has publicly identified him as Sulliman Bah. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the shooting happened last Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp during a gathering of roughly 100 teenagers. No arrests have been made, and Flowers said self-defense is a factor investigators are weighing as the case continues.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing Bah approaching a pickup truck occupied by two 18-year-olds. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed (the) 17-year-old in this case," Flowers said.

Flowers said the two teenagers who were inside the truck, including the person investigators say fired the shot, have been cooperating with law enforcement. "They turned over the weapon. They turned over the truck. They've been talking to our detectives all weekend. They're still here talking to us now," Flowers said. "So, it's going to be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed. But I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these."

Flowers said large teenage gatherings have become a growing concern for law enforcement and often form through social media platforms such as Snapchat. "This has been going on for a long time, but now we're adding guns into the mix and we're adding social media into the mix," Flowers said. "And so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains ongoing and is asking anyone with information about the shooting to come forward.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Video Shows Teen Punching Before Fatal Garcia's Boat Ramp Shooting
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said video evidence shows the 17-year-old killed Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp was throwing punches at people inside a truck moments before he was shot. The teen died following a confrontation at the waterfront site, which authorities say has become a popular gathering spot for teenagers, and investigators are now examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense.

Flowers described the video during a news conference, saying investigators reviewed footage showing the teen open the door of a truck and begin punching the occupants inside. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video showing the confrontation moments before the shooting.

Authorities said both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved. As of Monday, no arrests had been made. Flowers said it will be up to the state attorney's office to decide whether charges are filed. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," he said.

Flowers also addressed the broader pattern of large teen gatherings organized through social media at locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp, warning that the combination of firearms and these meetups is dangerous. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." He urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as a safety measure. The investigation remains active, and the sheriff's office is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

cards.headline: New I-95 Interchange at Oslo Road Opens 400 Days Early in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis celebrated the $100 million interchange, the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years, projected to cut emergency response times by as much as 56%.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis was in Indian River County on Monday to celebrate the completion of a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, a $100 million project state officials say will improve traffic flow, emergency response times and freight movement. The interchange opened about a year ahead of schedule and marks the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.

DeSantis said the project provides a new direct connection to I-95 while easing congestion at nearby interchanges at Indrio Road and State Road 60. "This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit," DeSantis said. Drivers using Oslo Road to access I-95 can expect travel times to be cut roughly in half, according to the governor. State transportation officials project traffic along the corridor will continue growing through 2045.

DeSantis said the project is expected to have significant public safety benefits as well. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could be reduced by as much as 56%, allowing first responders to reach crashes and other emergencies more quickly. "This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations," DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said improved access to I-95 for first responders was one of the project's most important features. "Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. The new interchange is also expected to improve freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County by providing a more direct route to the interstate for trucks and commercial traffic.

State officials said the project was accelerated through Florida's Moving Florida Forward initiative, a transportation funding program launched by the DeSantis administration to speed up major road projects across the state. Perdue said the Florida Department of Transportation worked with contractors through a "voluntary acceleration" program that rewarded construction teams for finding ways to complete projects more quickly, resulting in the Oslo Road interchange finishing approximately 400 days ahead of schedule. The department also acquired land near the interchange to establish a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which officials said will serve as the only relocation area of its kind in Southeast Florida, allowing protected tortoises to be moved while infrastructure projects continue. The Oslo Road interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across Florida's Treasure Coast region. "This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future," DeSantis said.

hero.body:

Deputies had already broken up a similar gathering earlier that night before the crowd moved to the ramp. The teen opened the truck door and began punching one of the occupants, and a shot from inside the truck struck and killed him. cards.headline: New $100M I-95 Oslo Road Interchange Opens 400 Days Early in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis joined state officials in Indian River County to celebrate the opening of a new $100 million I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, the first new interchange built on that stretch of I-95 in nearly 50 years.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis was in Indian River County on Monday to celebrate the completion of a new $100 million I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, a project state officials say will improve traffic flow, emergency response times and freight movement in the southern part of the county. The interchange opened about a year ahead of schedule and marks the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.

DeSantis said the project creates a new direct connection to I-95 while easing congestion at nearby interchanges at Indrio Road and State Road 60. "This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit," DeSantis said. He said drivers using Oslo Road to access I-95 can expect travel times to be cut roughly in half, and state transportation officials project traffic along the corridor will keep growing through 2045.

DeSantis said the project carries significant public safety benefits. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could drop by as much as 56%, helping first responders reach crashes and other emergencies faster. "This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations," DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said improved interstate access for first responders was one of the project's most important features. "Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. The interchange is also expected to improve freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County by giving trucks and commercial traffic a more direct route to the interstate.

State officials said the project was accelerated through Florida's Moving Florida Forward initiative, a transportation funding program launched by the DeSantis administration to speed up major road projects statewide. Perdue said FDOT worked with contractors through a "voluntary acceleration" program that rewarded construction teams for finishing work faster, allowing the Oslo Road interchange to be completed about 400 days ahead of schedule. FDOT also acquired land near the interchange to establish a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which officials said will serve as the only relocation area of its kind in Southeast Florida, allowing protected tortoises to be moved while infrastructure work continues. The Oslo Road interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across Florida's Treasure Coast region. "This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future," DeSantis said.

hero.headline: Florida Realtors' $18 Million Gives Amendment 3 a 26-to-1 Spending Edge Over Opponents
hero.body:
The political committee backing Amendment 3, which would raise Florida's homestead tax exemption, took in an $18 million cash infusion in September, according to newly disclosed campaign finance records. The two committees opposing the amendment raised a combined $680,000, giving supporters a spending advantage of more than 26 to 1. Voters can expect a surge of messaging in the coming days and weeks urging a "yes" vote on the measure.

The $18 million behind "Yes on 3" came from a single source: Florida Realtors. Margy Grant, chief executive of Florida Realtors, is the sole contributor to the committee. "As the voice of real estate, Florida Realtors is a longtime advocate for homeowners," Grant said. "Families are struggling with the affordability of so many things. When you go to the grocery store, when you go to the gas station, prices just continue to climb. The one thing we can possibly control is property taxes." By contrast, the "No" committees drew donations from a range of corporate, individual and nonprofit contributors.

Jackson Peel, spokesman for the "No" group Floridians for Shared Prosperity, said his side holds an advantage despite the funding gap. "Well, we have the advantage of the facts on our side," Peel said. "This is not the savings that is promised on the mailers in your mailbox from the realtors, that this is a scam and a tax shift. You're gonna end up paying more in other ways." Peel said opposition messaging is still reaching voters through groups including the Florida Sheriffs Association and the Florida Professional Firefighters. "I'm on the side of the sheriffs, the police, and the firefighters who say that this is bad for our community's public safety," Peel said. "I'm on the side of the teachers who say, yeah, this is gonna cut after-school programs that help our kids."

On concerns about funding for public services if the exemption increases, Grant said she trusts elected officials to manage the impact. "If you look at the increase in revenue over the past 10 years, it has doubled. Services have not doubled," Grant said. "I have full faith and confidence in our elected officials that they will be able to implement Amendment 3 successfully and effectively."

A constitutional amendment needs support from 60 percent of voters to pass in Florida. A Pete Polls survey found 45 percent of likely voters currently support Amendment 3, 30 percent oppose it, and 25 percent remain undecided, leaving supporters well short of the threshold with their financial advantage intact heading into the final stretch of the campaign.

"But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there."Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger."Now we're adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead."The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention."The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that," Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups."With Vero Beach High School's homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children's whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff's office."Parents, if your kids are telling you that they're headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they're going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us," Flowers said.He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place.The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward."I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people," Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they're going to have to be accountable for that."Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

hero.headline: New I-95 Oslo Road Interchange Opens a Year Early in Indian River County
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis opened a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County on Monday, a roughly $100 million project that was completed one year ahead of schedule. The Florida Department of Transportation and the governor's office said the interchange is the first new one built in the area in almost 50 years. DeSantis said it will cut travel times in half for drivers heading from Oslo Road to I-95 and will ease congestion at the nearby Indrio Road and State Road 60 interchanges.

DeSantis said the direct interstate connection will also speed up emergency response in southern Indian River County. "We anticipate that just for the local community on a normal basis, for local, like non-hurricane-type emergencies, that the emergency response time will be reduced by up to 56%," DeSantis said. "That will ultimately save some lives, of course, because time is of the essence in some of these situations."

FDOT Secretary Jared Perdue said the project finished 400 days ahead of its original timeline through a process the agency calls voluntary acceleration, which allows contractors to propose faster construction methods and share in the resulting savings. "This is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. "We're really excited about that, to include cutting commute time in half and so many other benefits." DeSantis said the number of daily vehicles on the corridor is expected to keep growing through 2045, and he called the Oslo Road interchange an example of infrastructure that improves quality of life now while building capacity for the future.

DeSantis said FDOT also acquired land near the interchange to create a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which he said will be the only relocation site of its kind in Southeast Florida. "Florida [is] showing that it's possible to do the projects that we need done while also buttressing environmental stewardship," DeSantis said. Perdue said nearly $1 billion in transportation investment is planned across the Treasure Coast region.

hero.headline: Man Booked in Indian River County Jail in Vero Beach Ex-Girlfriend's Killing
hero.body:
A man accused of crossing state lines to kill his ex-girlfriend in Vero Beach was booked into the Indian River County Jail early Monday on a charge of first-degree murder. Jail records show Matthew Waggle, 33, was booked at around 5:20 a.m. Waggle is accused of killing Dawn Kriskewic outside her home in the southern part of the county on a Sunday morning in August.

Investigators say Waggle traveled from out of state by bus and Uber to reach Vero Beach before the killing. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said surveillance video captured Waggle walking through Kriskewic's neighborhood shortly after an Uber dropped him off near her home. Authorities say he then took another Uber back to Orlando and boarded a Greyhound bus, eventually making his way to West Virginia, where he hid out at a motel.

Flowers said Flock Safety cameras were instrumental in tracking Waggle's movements after the killing. Investigators used that evidence to eventually locate him at the motel in West Virginia, where he was taken into custody.

Authorities said Kriskewic had ended her relationship with Waggle before she was killed. She had warned coworkers at the hair salon where she worked that she wanted no contact with him. Her body was found in a roadway in the southern part of Indian River County after the shooting.

hero.headline: Updated St. Lucie Cancer Data Shows No Elevated Rates as Families Keep Mapping Brain Tumors
hero.body:
An updated St. Lucie County Health Department analysis of cancer registry data through 2023 shows no indication of higher brain cancer rates in the county or in the specific ZIP codes families have been asking about, according to St. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber. The finding stands in contrast to the ongoing work of Stephanie Ankiel, a Fort Pierce widow who has spent years mapping brain cancer diagnoses street by street, including cases in homes just doors apart from each other.

Ankiel's own family is part of her map. She pointed to her late husband Mark Cunningham's childhood home in Fort Pierce, noting that another resident a few houses away was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor Cunningham first had, oligodendroglioma, before his cancer progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets over, she identified a home where two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma 20 years apart, and elsewhere along her route she pointed to neighboring homes where a woman and an 18-year-old were each diagnosed with brain cancer. Three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone in the areas families are tracking, though officials say the diagnoses and proximity of patients' homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause. Ankiel, who helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast, wants officials to examine the full range of brain cancers on her map rather than focusing on glioblastoma alone, noting that CDC guidance allows consideration of different cancer types when evidence suggests shared causes or exposures. No such connection has been established among the cases she is tracking.

Sperber wrote that the county's rates are in line with nearby counties and the state as a whole, and said officials were finishing a summary of the updated findings to post online. A 2019 Florida Department of Health review had examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983, finding no statistically significant increase and declining to designate a cancer cluster, but that review did not include diagnoses after 2017 or the broader range of brain tumors Ankiel is now tracking.

Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and release the data behind its conclusions. "You need to give us the receipts," Mast said. "Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place." The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns and confirmed it assisted Florida's investigation in 2018, but it did not address whether it had received Mast's latest request or would open a new review. A CDC spokesperson said the agency is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health's request.

Among those watching for answers is Matt Elliott, a former bar manager diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, an aggressive grade 4 brain cancer. Elliott said he initially believed his diagnosis was isolated until he met other local patients. He has decided not to continue treatment and is instead spending his time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. "I'm not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old," Elliott said. "But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun."

hero.headline: 17-Year-Old Dies After Shooting Near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 17-year-old boy has died after being shot late Friday night near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he later died from his injuries.

Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near the boat ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. Friday. Arriving deputies found the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived on scene.

Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division, along with crime scene personnel, are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and that there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released.

The investigation remains active. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Seniors Push Back as Orange Avenue Center Sale Nears
hero.body:
The Council on Aging of St. Lucie has confirmed that the senior center at 1505 Orange Avenue in Fort Pierce is expected to close as the property, currently listed for sale at $2.2 million, moves toward a sale. No timeline for the closure has been finalized because the transition depends on when the property sells. Services at the Orange Avenue center are continuing in the meantime.

The news caught some regular visitors off guard, including 77-year-old Sandy Pietrewicz, who has used the center for nearly a decade. "That's the community center that I go to for lunch and friendship and social activities with other elderly women," Pietrewicz said. She said she and other seniors began asking each other who they could contact for answers once they heard the center might close.

The Council on Aging said the closure will not end the services seniors currently receive. "You're going to get the same treatment. You're going to get the same love. You're going to get the same meals," said Trekina Smith with the Council on Aging. Once the Orange Avenue property sells, seniors are expected to transition to the organization's facility on Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie, with transportation provided to help them get there. The Council on Aging said seniors will keep access to meals, activities, social opportunities and transportation at the new location.

But for many seniors, the location itself is the issue. "That makes us even angrier. We can't have something in our own community," Pietrewicz said. Geneira Lovett, another regular at the center, said seniors in Fort Pierce want services close to home. "We live here, we want rights to do thing, besides trouble," Lovett said. The Council on Aging said it understands those concerns but maintains the change is necessary. "We understand the concerns, it's a change for us too. But hey, change comes, and you got to go with the change," Smith said.

His response did not explain how the analysis treated tumors initially diagnosed as one type and later reclassified as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers beyond glioblastoma were examined separately.

The state's earlier 2019 review looked only at glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983, and it found no statistically significant increase and did not designate a cancer cluster. That review did not include diagnoses after 2017 and did not look at the broader range of brain tumors that Stephanie Ankiel has mapped across Fort Pierce neighborhoods. Ankiel, who helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast, lost her husband, Mark Cunningham, to cancer that began as oligodendroglioma and later progressed to glioblastoma. During a drive through Fort Pierce, she pointed to the house where he grew up and, a few doors away, a home where she said another man was diagnosed in 2025 with the same initial tumor type. She also identified a home where two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma 20 years apart, and nearby houses where she said a woman and an 18-year-old were each diagnosed with brain cancer.

Ankiel said three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone among families she is tracking. She wants officials to study the full range of brain cancers on her map rather than glioblastoma alone, saying the area has too much brain cancer regardless of the specific diagnosis. CDC guidance allows different cancer types to be considered together when evidence points to shared causes or exposures, but no such connection has been established among the cases Ankiel and other families are following, and the clustering of diagnoses does not by itself establish a common cause.

Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and release the data behind its conclusions, saying officials need to provide the receipts showing where the cases took place and how many there were. The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns and confirmed it assisted Florida's investigation in 2018, but it did not say whether it had received Mast's latest request or would open a new review. A CDC spokesperson said the agency is prepared to provide additional assistance if the Florida Department of Health requests it. Matt Elliott, diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, said he once believed his case was isolated until meeting other local patients changed his mind. He has decided not to pursue further treatment and is instead spending his time with friends and family, including trips to the beach, while he hopes investigators eventually find answers.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Man Charged After Ramming Two Tow Trucks With U-Haul
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce Police say a man rammed a U-Haul truck into two tow trucks on Jamboree Drive during a dispute over an HOA-ordered tow, freeing the vehicle before officers tracked him down nearby.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man is facing an aggravated assault charge after police say he rammed two tow trucks with a U-Haul box truck during a dispute over a homeowner association ordered tow. Fort Pierce Police officers responded Thursday to the 5400 block of Jamboree Drive, east of Interstate 95, after reports that the U-Haul had crashed into two vehicles.

Officers learned the U-Haul had been parked in violation of homeowner association restrictions and that a contracted tow company was attempting to remove it. According to police, the man intervened during the tow attempt. A second tow truck had been positioned behind the U-Haul to keep it from leaving the scene.

Police said the man refused to pay a drop fee, then got into the U-Haul, backed off the first tow truck and struck the one parked behind him. He continued driving forward and in reverse repeatedly until he freed the U-Haul from between the two vehicles, police said, then drove off down the street.

Responding officers located the man shortly afterward. No injuries were reported in the incident. The U-Haul was towed from the scene, and the man was taken into custody on the aggravated assault charge. Police did not identify him.

hero.headline: Indiantown Flooding Persists Despite $2M Booker Park Drainage Project
hero.body:
Flooding returned to Indiantown streets last week after heavy rain, and residents are bracing for more water as additional rain and storms are forecast this week. Vehicles were seen driving through standing water on village roadways, renewing frustration over a drainage and roadway project in Booker Park that has cost more than $2 million. The project began in 2022 to help reduce flooding in the area, but residents say heavy rain still leaves some streets underwater.

Mary Brown, a Booker Park resident, said the financial toll of repeated flooding falls hardest on those without insurance. "The sad part is, if you don't have insurance or anything like that you're just stuck, your stuck with the bill," Brown said. Village leaders have said they are working with Martin County on longer-term drainage solutions, including the possible repair or replacement of broken pipes. The next Indiantown Village Council meeting is scheduled for Thursday night.

With more rain possible this week, Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Department of Health in Martin County are urging residents to plan ahead and avoid driving or walking through floodwater. Officials say water on a roadway may be deeper or more contaminated than it appears, and drivers who encounter a flooded road should turn around rather than attempt to drive through it. Martin County Fire Rescue responds to flooding-related emergencies, including cases where a vehicle becomes stuck in floodwater, and residents should call 911 during an emergency.

For ongoing drainage problems or flooded roadways that are not emergencies, residents can submit a report through Martin County's online Request for Service system. The county asks that reports include the specific address or location along with details about the issue, such as standing water, a blockage or a low spot near a drainage structure. Health officials also advise residents whose wells flood to use bottled or boiled water until the well can be tested.

hero.headline: Teen Dies After Late-Night Shooting Near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Fellsmere
hero.body:
A 17-year-old boy died after being shot Friday night near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Fellsmere, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said. Deputies responded around 11:24 p.m. to reports of a juvenile who had been shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the area where the boat ramp is located.

Deputies found the teen at the scene and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived, according to the sheriff's office. He was first taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he later died from his injuries.

Detectives with the sheriff's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the area and interviewing multiple witnesses. The sheriff's office said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and that there is no threat to the public. The investigation remains active.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The sheriff's office said additional information will be released as it becomes available.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach Septic Backups Persist as Sewer Conversion Date Stays Unset
hero.body:
Residents on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach say heavy rain still sends sewage from their septic tanks up into their yards, a recurring problem that has left them without working toilets for days at a time. Martin County staff confirm the neighborhood remains on the list for septic-to-sewer conversion, but no firm date has been set for the work, even as residents continue to deal with the health and sanitation fallout after every significant storm.

Daniel Fletchall, who lives on Northwest Sunset Boulevard, said the backups force sewage out of his tank and into his yard. "The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard," Fletchall said. "It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out." Fletchall said the problem can leave his household unable to flush toilets for days, forcing him to find other options. "I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom," he said. He added that he also cannot shower or wash clothes at home during these periods. "Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower," Fletchall said. "But it's just not happening here."

Fletchall is not alone. Neighbor Christie Berger said she faces the same issue every time it rains heavily, telling WPTV she sometimes has to go to a nearby McDonald's to use the bathroom. Another neighbor, Rachelle Kukan, said the situation has become unbearable. "I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could," Kukan said. Fletchall said he has brought in septic companies to address drainage in his yard, but was told that elevating his septic tank would be costly and still might not fix the underlying problem. He said he wants Martin County to extend sewer lines into the neighborhood. "I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but I'm not getting any help here," Fletchall said.

Martin County staff said the Northwest Sunset Boulevard neighborhood is included on the county's list for septic-to-sewer conversion, but they have not set a timeline for when that work would begin. Staff said they are exploring ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems slated for conversion. Until that happens, residents say they will keep relying on public restrooms and family members' homes to avoid the sewage problems in their own yards after every heavy rain.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Man Gets 37.5 Years for Stuart Vape Shop Shooting
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison for a January 2025 shooting at a Stuart vape shop. Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger sentenced Joshua Gibbs on Tuesday to the prison term plus 10 years of probation to follow his release, Stuart police said Friday. Gibbs had changed his plea to guilty on five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing a mask, shooting a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon.

The case began when Gibbs was denied service at Miller's Vapory, at 1596 SE Federal Highway, for being underage. A month later, on Jan. 25, 2025, deputies responded to a shooting at the store at 7:31 p.m. Police said Gibbs entered wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun, then opened fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire, and no one was injured. Gibbs had threatened the clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," before stealing about $300 worth of merchandise and leaving the area.

Stuart Police detectives launched an extensive investigation to identify the shooter. A person matching Gibbs' description was later spotted riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, close to an address where records showed he had once lived. His arrest report also listed an address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live.

A warrant was issued for Gibbs' arrest, and he was eventually captured in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. He was brought back to face charges in St. Lucie County and ultimately pleaded guilty, closing out a case that started with a dispute over an underage sale and ended in a gunfight at the Stuart shop.

cards.headline: Eight Months Later, Family Still Searching for Missing Port St. Lucie Father
cards.teaser: Robert La Polla's sister is renewing her public plea eight months after the Port St. Lucie father vanished following a hospital release in Fort Pierce, as detectives continue an unsolved search.
cards.body:
It has been eight months since Robert La Polla, a 47-year-old Port St. Lucie father, disappeared after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce on Jan. 8. He has not been seen or heard from since, and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office says the case remains unsolved with no confirmed sightings.

"I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, La Polla's sister, who continues to publicly plead for information as the milestone passes. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression after their parents died, but the siblings stayed close and spoke often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother vanishing without a trace is completely out of character.

In the months since La Polla disappeared, family members and friends have organized repeated search efforts across Fort Pierce, combing wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The toll of the search has extended to La Polla's young daughter, who is still waiting for her father to come home. "She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him."

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has entered La Polla into a national missing persons database. Investigators have collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and say they continue to follow up on leads, though the case remains inconclusive eight months later. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Man Gets 37.5 Years in Stuart Vape Shop Shooting
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison for a January 2025 shooting at a Stuart vape shop, Stuart police said Friday. Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger sentenced Joshua Gibbs on Tuesday and added 10 years of probation to follow his prison term. Gibbs had changed his plea to guilty on five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing a mask, shooting with a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon.

The shooting happened at 7:31 p.m. on Jan. 25, 2025, at Miller's Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the store wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun, then opened fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire, and no one was injured. Gibbs had been denied service at the store one month earlier for being underage. During the confrontation, he threatened the clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," before stealing $300 worth of merchandise and fleeing.

Stuart police detectives carried out an extensive investigation before identifying Gibbs as the suspect. Investigators found a person matching his description riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, close to where records showed he had once lived. His arrest report also listed an address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live.

A warrant was issued for Gibbs' arrest, and he was ultimately captured in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. He now faces decades behind bars followed by a decade of probation for the shooting that police say could have ended far worse for the clerk who returned fire.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District Attorney Resigns Amid Hazing Scandal
cards.teaser: Sabol submitted her 90-day resignation notice as fired firefighters fight their terminations and the fire board moves to overhaul how complaints are handled.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District attorney, Sabol, has submitted her 90-day notice of resignation, effective Wednesday. The district said it would not speculate on what led to her decision, but the resignation comes amid hazing allegations that have roiled the department.

Three firefighters were fired over what the district described as hazing. Video appears to show them shocking their coworkers with a modified bug zapper. The fired firefighters are now fighting to get their jobs back, claiming the terminations were retaliation for complaints they filed against district leadership.

St. Lucie County Fire Board members are working to create a new complaint review policy covering fire department leadership. At a meeting Wednesday night, officials decided to reach out to outside law firms to serve as a third party in developing a new complaint structure for the district.

The board's move to bring in outside legal help comes as the district faces questions over how it handled the hazing complaints and the firefighters' subsequent firings. It was not immediately clear when the district expects to select a firm or finalize the new policy.

hero.headline: 17-Year-Old Killed in Shooting Near Vero Beach Boat Ramp, Deputies Seek Witnesses
hero.body:
A 17-year-old boy was shot and killed Friday night near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Vero Beach, and detectives with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office are actively investigating the homicide while seeking witnesses. Deputies responded around 11:24 p.m. Friday to reports of a juvenile who had been shot in the area of the boat ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512.

Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived, according to the sheriff's office. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he later died from his injuries.

Detectives with the sheriff's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the area and interviewing multiple witnesses. The sheriff's office said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public, though the investigation remains active.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The sheriff's office said additional information will be released as it becomes available.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mosquito Crews Treat Standing Water Near U.S. 1 in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County mosquito control teams are treating standing water left by recent heavy rain in a Fort Pierce neighborhood, warning that mosquito populations could spike quickly. Crews are urging residents to dump or remove any containers holding water around their homes.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County mosquito control crews are treating swales and other standing water in a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 in Fort Pierce after recent heavy rain left pools of water where mosquitoes can breed. Teams used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide in the area, part of an active effort to stop mosquito eggs from hatching before populations grow.

Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control, said the rain has created more standing water than usual, which gives mosquito eggs the conditions they need to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment's notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," Tuzzolino said. He said more rain is expected in the coming days, which could lead to even more standing water and, in his words, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!"

Kenneth Fusco, who lives nearby, described the toll the mosquitoes have taken on daily life outdoors. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He also asked drivers to avoid lingering near his home. "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" he said.

Mosquito control officials are asking residents across St. Lucie County to empty or remove any containers around their homes that can collect water, a practice they call "tip and toss." "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. Separately, Thursday's heavy rain caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project meant to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. Residents dealing with mosquito problems near their homes can contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or by email at mosquito@stlucieco.org.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Teen Enrique Rosario Liz Named National Youth of the Year
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz won the Boys & Girls Clubs of America's top national honor this week, and a hometown welcome celebration is planned at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
The Boys & Girls Clubs of America has named a St. Lucie County teen its 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, the organization's highest honor for a club member. Enrique Rosario Liz received the award during a national ceremony in New York City on Thursday night after representing Florida and the Southeast Region in the competition. A welcome-home celebration for Rosario Liz is planned for 7 p.m. Friday at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport.

According to the Boys & Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County, Rosario Liz first won local and state Youth of the Year titles before advancing to the national level. He moved to the United States from the Dominican Republic when he was 8 years old. Club leaders said he later created a Spanish class for younger members at the club.

Rosario Liz graduated as valedictorian from Port St. Lucie High School and is now studying elementary education at the University of Florida. The Youth of the Year program recognizes Boys & Girls Club members for leadership, service, academic success and commitment to their communities.

The welcome-home celebration at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport will give the St. Lucie County community a chance to honor Rosario Liz's achievement in person following his trip to New York City for the national ceremony.

hero.headline: Two Miami Women Charged After Gunfire, Chase at Martin County Tow Yard
hero.body:
Two women from Miami are facing charges after a dispute over guns in a repossessed car turned into gunfire at a Martin County tow yard, a high-speed chase and a crash that triggered a lockout at a nearby middle school Friday afternoon. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary's Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other people showed up to claim the same vehicle. "They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns," Budensiek said. One of the original women grabbed a gun and opened fire. No one was hurt, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, was not at the scene when the shooting happened but said an employee called him screaming for help. "It's just crazy how it went down," Reed said. "And I'm running as fast as I can."

By the time deputies and Reed reached the tow yard, all four people involved had fled. hero.headline: Second Arrest Made in Stuart Tow Yard Shooting, Chase and Crash
hero.body:
Martin County deputies have arrested a second woman in connection with Friday's shooting at a Stuart tow yard that triggered a school lockout, a police pursuit and multiple crashes. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said 24-year-old Valerie Valdes accompanied 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, to Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road, where Rondon had gone to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier Friday. Deputies said another group arrived at the tow yard shortly afterward, leading to an altercation in which Rondon pulled out a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing in a vehicle. Rondon was arrested after a pursuit and is charged with two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended and felony criminal mischief.

Because the tow yard sits about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while they searched for the suspect. The school sent a message to families saying, "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth."

Deputies said Valdes fled the tow yard in the vehicle she and Rondon had originally arrived in. Sheriff John Budensiek said, "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash." Investigators said Valdes crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. 1. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries.

Separately, deputies located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to take her into custody. The people allegedly targeted in the shooting had left the tow yard before deputies arrived. Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, said he was grateful no one at the business was hurt, adding, "I love all the people around me. Even the people next door." The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges against either woman are possible.

hero.headline: 17-Year-Old Dies After Shooting Near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 17-year-old boy died after a shooting late Friday night near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. The Indian River School District confirmed the teen had recently withdrawn from Sebastian River High School to be homeschooled and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting.

Deputies responded at 11:24 p.m. to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area between Fellsmere and Vero Beach. Deputies found the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said.

District spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement that the district is "deeply saddened by the loss of this young person," adding that "our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community." In a follow-up email, Schafte wrote, "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time."

Lt. Kevin Jaworski of the sheriff's office said in an alert to media that the shooting "appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," calling it "an active investigation." He said investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel processed the scene and interviewed multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Man Gets 37.5 Years for Stuart Vape Shop Shooting
hero.teaser: Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison plus 10 years of probation for a masked shooting and robbery attempt at a Stuart vape shop that touched off a multi-state manhunt.
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison for a January 2025 shooting and attempted robbery at a Stuart vape shop. Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger sentenced Joshua Gibbs on Tuesday to the prison term followed by 10 years of probation, Stuart police said Friday.

Gibbs changed his plea to guilty on five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing a mask, shooting with a deadly missile, and carrying a concealed weapon.

Stuart police said deputies responded to a shooting at 7:31 p.m. on Jan. 25, 2025, at Miller's Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the business wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun, then opened fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire and no one was injured. Police said Gibbs had been denied service at the shop a month earlier for being underage. During the incident, Gibbs threatened the clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," then stole about $300 worth of merchandise before leaving.

After an extensive investigation, Stuart Police detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect. Investigators found a person matching his description riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, close to where records showed he once lived. His arrest report also listed an address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live. A warrant was issued for his arrest, and he was apprehended in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force.
