hero.headline: Charges Filed After Stuart Tow Yard Shooting Triggered School Lockout, Chase
hero.body:
Two Miami women face charges after a shooting Friday afternoon at Garry's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road in Martin County that triggered a lockout at nearby Murray Middle School, a police chase and a separate crash. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says more charges could be coming as detectives continue investigating.

Sheriff John Budensiek said the case began with a car that had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening and was then reported stolen. Detectives recovered the car at the tow yard Friday morning. Around 1 p.m., Jade Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard with another woman, Valerie Valdes, to retrieve it. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived, and the two parties got into an altercation. "They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns," Budensiek said. Rondon then got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into her car and leaving. The people who were shot at also left before deputies arrived.

Garry Reed, owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said an employee in his office was badly shaken. "Young lady who works in my office, she was terrorized," Reed said. He said his business had helped the Sheriff's Office recover the car that morning, and the situation turned dangerous when the car's owner came to pick it up that afternoon. "The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire," Reed said. "Scary. I'm racing, my heart is racing," he said.

Because the tow yard sits near Murray Middle School, the Sheriff's Office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. Road patrol deputies, aviation units, detectives and other personnel searched for Rondon's car and located it on Cove Road near US-1. When deputies tried to stop her, she fled, and deputies performed a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. Valdes was later involved in a separate incident, driving recklessly and losing control in a crash near Osprey Street and US-1. No one was seriously hurt in either incident.

Rondon faces two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving with a suspended license and felony criminal mischief. Valdes faces charges of operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The Sheriff's Office is still executing search warrants and reviewing data and video evidence to determine exactly what happened. "We're honestly not sure what we have," Budensiek said. "We're sure that shots are fired. We're sure that she fled from our deputies. Something happened with that vehicle the night before. There was a reason why everyone had interest in that car." Reed said he is grateful no one was killed. "Thank God that everybody was okay," he said.

hero.headline: Stuart Tow Yard Shooting Sparks Murray Middle Lockout, Two Arrests
hero.body:
A shooting at a Martin County tow yard triggered a lockout at nearby Murray Middle School, a police pursuit that ended in a PIT maneuver, and a separate injury crash, leading to the arrest of two women on Friday. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the incident began shortly after 1 p.m. at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road.

Investigators said 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business sits about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Murray Middle School sent a message to families that read in part, "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth"

Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief.

According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle the two women originally arrived in and drove recklessly while attempting to leave the area. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. 1. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, said he is grateful no one was hurt during the incident. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

cards.headline: Martin County Sheriff: Questions Remain in Stuart Tow Yard Shooting Case
cards.teaser: Two women are in custody after a shooting at a Stuart tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash, but Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek says investigators still have unanswered questions.
cards.body:
Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard in Stuart led to a police chase and a violent crash. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek says investigators are still working to answer key questions about the case, including why one of the suspects was driving recklessly before her arrest.

Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. "They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns," Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard.

Gary Reed, the owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, said he was not present during the shooting but got a call from an employee screaming for help. "It's just crazy how it went down," Reed said. By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. Budensiek said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing over, but deputies located her shortly after. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, also from Miami. Budensiek said Valdes was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. Highway.

"Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we're not sure. We didn't even know for sure that that car was involved at that time," Budensiek said. "I have more questions than I have answers," he said. The sheriff said investigators plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects' cars and phones as they continue working to answer those questions. Budensiek said he hopes to have more answers by next week.

hero.headline: Two Miami Women Charged After Tow Yard Shooting Near Stuart Sparks School Lockout
hero.body:
Two Miami women are facing charges following a shooting Friday afternoon at a tow yard near Stuart that triggered a lockout at a nearby middle school and ended with a crash and a PIT maneuver by Martin County deputies, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Jade Ely Brandon, 23, is charged with two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended and felony criminal mischief. Sheriff John Budensiek said Valerie Valdes, 22, caused a crash while fleeing the scene and faces charges of operating an unregistered motorcycle vehicle and reckless driving with injuries.

Deputies were called to Gary's Towing and Recovery at 4405 SE Cove Road around 1 p.m. Brandon had gone to the tow yard to retrieve a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day, arriving with Valdes. A short time later, two other people showed up to claim the same car, and an argument broke out among the four. According to the sheriff's office, Brandon grabbed a gun and opened fire before getting into a vehicle with Valdes and fleeing the area. Budensiek said some of the gunfire struck a trailer where tow yard employees were working at the time. "They're extremely fortunate just doing their job, minding their own business," the sheriff said. "They've got a lot going on."

Because the tow yard sits about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office activated an active-shooter protocol and placed the school on lockout while deputies responded. Road patrol units, aviation support, detectives and other personnel began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies eventually spotted it traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and tried to initiate a traffic stop. The driver refused to pull over, prompting deputies to perform a Precision Immobilization Technique, or PIT maneuver, which brought the vehicle to a stop. Additional units then moved in to fully immobilize the car before the driver could attempt to flee again. Budensiek noted that both the tow yard employees and those involved in the confrontation were fortunate no one was seriously hurt given the circumstances. The investigation into the shooting and the events leading up to the chase remains ongoing as authorities continue to piece together what sparked the dispute between the four individuals over the vehicle.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Teen Enrique Rosario Liz Named National Youth of the Year
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organization's 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others.

The honor caps a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, which advanced him to the national level of competition.

In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys & Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the news during a special presentation.

Now Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys & Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Man Gets 37.5 Years in Stuart Vape Shop Shooting
cards.teaser: Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison for a masked armed robbery and shootout at a Stuart vape shop in January 2025 that led to a multi-state manhunt.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison for a January 2025 masked armed robbery and shootout at a Stuart vape shop. Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger sentenced Joshua Gibbs on Tuesday, also ordering 10 years of probation following his time in state prison, Stuart police said Friday.

Gibbs changed his plea to guilty on five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing a mask, shooting with a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon. Deputies responded to a shooting at 7:31 p.m. on Jan. 25, 2025, at Miller's Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the business wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun before opening fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire and no one was injured.

One month before the shooting, Gibbs had been denied service at the shop for being underage. During the robbery, Gibbs threatened the store clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," then stole $300 worth of merchandise before leaving the area.

Stuart Police detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect after an extensive investigation. A person matching his description was spotted riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, near where records confirmed he lived at one time. The arrest report also listed an address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live. A warrant was issued for Gibbs, and he was apprehended in Douglasville, Georgia, with the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force on Feb. 2.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mosquito Crews Treat Standing Water Near U.S. 1 in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County mosquito control teams are treating standing water left by recent heavy rain in a Fort Pierce neighborhood, warning that mosquito populations could spike quickly.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County mosquito control crews are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain left standing water across the county, including in a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 in Fort Pierce. Crews treated swales in the area and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch.

Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control, said mosquito calls have been down compared to last year but conditions can change fast. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment's notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," Tuzzolino said. More rain is expected, which Tuzzolino said could bring a fresh surge in mosquitoes. "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" he said.

Kenneth Fusco, who lives near the affected area, described dealing with the mosquitoes outside his own home. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added a request for mosquito control trucks spraying in his neighborhood: "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!"

Mosquito control crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. Tuzzolino urged residents to empty or remove any containers holding water around their homes to cut down on breeding grounds. "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were finishing a shoulder repair project meant to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. Residents dealing with mosquito problems near their homes can contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org.

Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. hero.headline: Second Arrest Made in Stuart Tow Yard Shooting That Locked Out Murray Middle School
hero.body:
A second woman has been arrested in connection with Friday's shooting at a Martin County tow yard that triggered a lockout at Murray Middle School and ended with a police pursuit and multiple crashes. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the incident began shortly after 1 p.m. at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road when 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation, and Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle.

Because the tow yard sits about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Murray Middle School sent parents a message that read in part, "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth." Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to take her into custody. Rondon faces charges of two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief.

A second suspect, 24-year-old Valerie Valdes, was arrested after the chaos spilled onto nearby roads. The sheriff's office said Valdes had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW, and after the shooting she fled in the vehicle the two women originally arrived in, driving recklessly as she tried to leave the area. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. 1. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries.

The people who were allegedly targeted by Rondon's gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived and have not been located. Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, said he is grateful no one was hurt during the incident. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and that additional charges are possible as detectives continue working to identify and locate the original targets of the shooting.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Residents Battle Repeated Septic Backups, Await Sewer Conversion
cards.teaser: Residents on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach say heavy rain repeatedly sends septic sewage into their yards, and Martin County confirms the neighborhood is on the list for septic-to-sewer conversion with no firm date set.
cards.body:
Residents on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach say heavy rain regularly causes their septic systems to back up into their yards and homes, and Martin County has confirmed the neighborhood is slated for septic-to-sewer conversion, though no timeline has been set. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall said the problem has become part of daily life. "The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard," Fletchall said. "It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out."

Fletchall said the backups force him and his family to avoid using their own plumbing for days at a time. "I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom," Fletchall said. He said he cannot shower or wash clothes at home during these periods, though he can shower at his parents' nearby house. "But it's just not happening here," Fletchall said.

Other neighbors on the street report the same problem after heavy rain. Christie Berger said she has had to find bathrooms elsewhere when her septic system backs up. "I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to," Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said the situation has become unbearable. "I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could," Kukan said.

Fletchall said he has had septic companies evaluate the drainage issues at his property. He said elevating his septic tank would be costly and might not even fix the problem. Fletchall said he wants Martin County to extend sewer lines into the neighborhood. "I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but I'm not getting any help here," Fletchall said. Martin County staff confirmed the Northwest Sunset Boulevard neighborhood is on the county's list for septic-to-sewer conversion, but said no date has been set for the work. Staff said the county is looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to be converted.

cards.headline: Palm City Woman Faces 72 Charges as Rescued Border Collies Find Homes
cards.teaser: Paige O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges in the case of 36 border collies rescued from her feces-filled Palm City home, with her next hearing set for December. Nearly all the dogs have since found homes through the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
A criminal case against Paige O'Donnell is moving forward nearly two months after Martin County deputies removed 36 border collies from her feces-filled home in Palm City. O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges, two for each dog rescued, including an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each animal. She has pleaded not guilty, and her next hearing is scheduled for December.

O'Donnell was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon at the Martin County courthouse. Her attorney, Russell Ferraro, said the defense team only recently received discovery materials in the case. "At this point I can't really say anything on her behalf for or against her," Ferraro said. "We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We're organizing it, going through it, and we'll take it from there." Ferraro added, "Everybody's got a right to a fair trial and to due process."

Martin County condemned O'Donnell's home days after deputies rescued the dogs in August. Ferraro said O'Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house undergoes repair.

While the criminal case continues, most of the rescued border collies have found new homes. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says 30 of the 36 dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Among the adopters are Cale and Colleen Tilley near Deltona, who each took in one of the dogs, now named Nadia and Leila. Cale said Nadia goes to work with him every day and has settled in with little trouble. "When I saw where they came from, I expected a lot more of a challenge," he said. Tilley described Leila as full of energy, saying "there's no off switch; it's all go, go, go." She said Leila was nervous when she first arrived in September but has since adjusted, now running through doors rather than hiding under the bed. Tilley, who showed dogs with her family as a child, said she remembered O'Donnell's reputation for well-bred, well-trained dogs and said she still wonders what went wrong. Cale said he adopted Nadia about a year after losing his previous border collie, Jessie, to cancer. "You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog," he said.

hero.headline: Fellsmere Rabies Alert Issued After Positive Bat Near Sonrise Apartments
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments in Fellsmere tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in September. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472.

The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure.

The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials recommend taking precautions to reduce the risk of exposure during the 60-day alert period covering the Fellsmere area.

Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Residents can visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

hero.headline: FDLE Agent Testifies on Missing Lincoln Theater Parking Language in Mimms Trial
hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms is standing trial in St. Lucie County on charges of bid tampering and official misconduct tied to a city bidding process for two vacant lots in Fort Pierce's Lincoln Park area. Mimms has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors allege he steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals, a nonprofit whose board included his niece and another city employee.

On Thursday, testimony from FDLE Agent Derek Brisky centered on who controlled the request for proposals process and how closely Mimms stayed involved after it moved to the city's purchasing department. Brisky testified that Mimms had told the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency the RFP would include language addressing parking needs for the nearby Lincoln Theater. Brisky also testified investigators found no evidence Mimms ever filed a 2019 memorandum concerning the parking plans in city records. Defense attorneys questioned the significance of the missing language and emphasized that the purchasing department, not Mimms, was responsible for assembling and publishing the RFP once it received project specifications.

Defense attorneys also challenged prosecutors' characterization of the process as a sole-source arrangement, and Brisky acknowledged the RFP was not technically a sole-source contract. Prosecutors pointed to emails showing Mimms continued communicating with city employees about the RFP after it left his office, including discussions of evaluation criteria and the evaluation committee. Other emails showed city employees were aware only one submission had come in after the RFP was posted, and an LPYP email address was copied on one of those communications. The defense also raised questions about how investigators treated other city employees involved in the process, including a purchasing official who was not charged.

Former Fort Pierce employee Kalita Scott also testified Thursday about LPYP and its efforts to develop the Lincoln Park properties. She described the organization as a group of young professionals focused on community development and said the need for parking near the Lincoln Theater was widely known in the community.

Prosecutors allege Mimms manipulated the city's process to ensure LPYP received the lease. The defense has argued Mimms did not improperly favor the organization and that the evidence presented does not establish a criminal conspiracy. The trial is continuing in St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Teen Wins National Youth of the Year, Set for Hometown Welcome
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, who moved to St. Lucie County from the Dominican Republic as a child, was named the Boys & Girls Clubs of America's 2026-27 National Youth of the Year. A welcome-home celebration for him is planned for 7 p.m. Friday at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County teen has been named the Boys & Girls Clubs of America's 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, the organization's highest honor for a club member. Enrique Rosario Liz received the award during a national ceremony in New York City on Thursday night after representing Florida and the Southeast Region in the competition. A welcome-home celebration for Enrique is planned for 7 p.m. Friday at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport.

According to the Boys & Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County, Enrique first won local and state Youth of the Year titles before advancing to the national level. He moved to the United States from the Dominican Republic when he was 8 years old. Club leaders said he later created a Spanish class for younger members at the club.

Enrique graduated as valedictorian from Port St. Lucie High School and is now studying elementary education at the University of Florida. Youth of the Year recognizes Boys & Girls Club members for leadership, service, academic success and commitment to their communities.

Friday's celebration at the airport will mark Enrique's return to St. Lucie County following the national ceremony.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Man Gets 37 1/2 Years in Stuart Vape Shop Shooting
cards.teaser: Joshua Gibbs was sentenced for a January 2025 shooting at a Stuart vape shop that began with a dispute over underage sales months earlier.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man has been sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison for a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop, according to the Stuart Police Department. Joshua Gibbs will also serve 10 years of probation after his prison term ends.

The sentence stems from a shooting on Jan. 25, 2025, at Miller's Vapory, located at 1596 SE Federal Highway in Stuart. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured in the exchange.

Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, according to police. He was arrested in Douglasville, Georgia, with assistance from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force.

Police said the shooting followed an earlier confrontation between Gibbs and the clerk in December 2024, after Gibbs was denied service for being underage. Investigators said Gibbs threatened the clerk during that encounter and stole more than $300 in vape products. He was initially charged with attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the December theft, before the January shooting led to the charges that resulted in his sentencing.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie TikTok Creator Jailed After Police Reopen Computer Access Case
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man whose TikTok bio describes him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed this week after detectives reopened an investigation into claims he accessed women's devices and posted their private information online.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man who identifies himself as a cybersecurity engineer on TikTok and Twitch was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped.

The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women's electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile's bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman.

Police said one video included references to a woman's password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts.

The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea's booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

cards.headline: Two Port St. Lucie Hit-and-Run Suspects Charged, Both Out on Bond
cards.teaser: A 23-year-old man is charged after a crash left a 16-year-old critically injured on Southwest Roma Way, while a 19-year-old faces charges after a high-speed chase that ended on Interstate 95.
cards.body:
Two men arrested this week in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases have both been released from jail on bond, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. One crash left a teenager critically injured, and the other followed a high-speed chase that ended on Interstate 95.

According to an arrest affidavit, 23-year-old Giovanny Barthelemy was driving a silver Toyota Highlander around 8:40 p.m. Tuesday when it collided with a 16-year-old riding an electric motorcycle on Southwest Roma Way near Southwest Lorenzo Way. A security camera at a community clubhouse recorded the crash, showing the SUV turning into the community entrance as the teen crossed in front of it. The teen was thrown from the motorcycle, and the affidavit says the SUV backed up and drove away while he lay on the ground waving his arms. The teen was taken to Tradition Medical Center and then flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where police said he broke his left femur and hurt his left ankle. He was listed in serious but stable condition. One witness told police the electric motorcycle had no headlights, and two witnesses said both vehicles were going fast. The SUV's owner, the father of Barthelemy's girlfriend, called 911 and told police Barthelemy said he had hit someone on a bike and then driven home. Officers found Barthelemy at his home on Southwest Ridgecrest Drive. After being read his rights, Barthelemy told police he felt and heard the crash and knew right away he had hit a person, and said he should have stopped but didn't, according to the affidavit. He told police his phone was dead. Barthelemy is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving injuries, a felony, and was given a traffic citation. He was released on a $7,500 bond.

The second case happened earlier the same afternoon. An officer clocked a silver Toyota going 85 mph in a 40-mph zone, according to an arrest affidavit. When the officer tried to stop the car, the driver went over a concrete median into oncoming lanes, ran a red light, and hit a traffic sign at Southwest Becker Road and Southwest Hallmark Street before getting on northbound Interstate 95. The officer turned off his lights and siren but kept the car in sight. The car later broke down on the side of I-95, and police said the driver, 19-year-old Christian Johnson, got out and ran toward the back of the car. A detective, a Florida Highway Patrol trooper, and the officer surrounded the car, and Johnson was taken into custody. According to the affidavit, Johnson's license had been suspended three times. Johnson is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, reckless driving, and driving with a suspended or revoked license, all misdemeanors. He was released on a $12,500 bond.

In a statement about both arrests, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said drivers are legally required to stop, whether it's for a traffic stop or after a crash. "Fleeing from law enforcement or leaving the scene of a crash can have serious consequences," the department said.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Repairs South Indian River Drive Erosion for Second Time in a Week
cards.teaser: Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to fix a washed-out embankment for the second time in a week, as residents push for a permanent fix like a seawall.
cards.body:
Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to repair a washed-out embankment for the second time in a week. King tides and recent rain continue to affect parts of South Florida, and the narrow roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon has taken the brunt of it. Skid loaders worked along the road adding dirt and sand to reinforce the area where erosion has left the edge of the pavement vulnerable. Crews brought 32 loads of dirt to the site in September, but only days later the embankment needed repairs again.

Resident Gene Barnes said the recurring work is not a long-term solution. "We're losing ground year by year," Barnes said. "Until the Corps of Engineers or something like that comes and puts a headwall in to stabilize it, it's not going to be an easy fix."

The road has faced erosion problems before. Heavy rain damaged sections of South Indian River Drive in 2014, and Hurricane Nicole caused additional washouts in 2022. Barnes said continued rain and tidal action could undermine the roadway itself. "If we keep getting rains like this, it's going to undermine the road, and then the road is going to collapse and the school bus is going to fall in the hole," he said.

The latest repairs follow an emergency sand operation at nearby Jetty Park that cost taxpayers nearly $500,000. Repairs on South Indian River Drive may be less costly, but residents said the erosion is likely to remain a concern as more rain and tidal action are forecast.

lead_independence.headline: Buc-ee's Clears All St. Lucie County Hurdles, Spurring Indrio Road Development Rush
lead_independence.lead: The proposed Buc-ee's travel center at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed St. Lucie County's planning process, clearing the way for construction once state approvals are finalized. St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer said the project is done with local review. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." The 76,000-square-foot travel center is planned to include about 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee's location in Florida. Balcer said the company is now waiting on final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before breaking ground. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date.

hero.headline: Two Port St. Lucie Hit-and-Run Suspects Arrested, Released on Bond
hero.body:
Two men are out of jail on bond after being arrested this week in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases, one of which left a 16-year-old boy seriously injured in the road, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Giovanny Barthelemy, 23, and Christian Johnson, 19, each face charges after fleeing the scenes of their crashes, and police say both have since posted bond.

According to an arrest affidavit, Barthelemy was driving a silver Toyota Highlander around 8:40 p.m. Tuesday when it collided with a 16-year-old riding an electric motorcycle on Southwest Roma Way near Southwest Lorenzo Way. A security camera at a nearby community clubhouse recorded the crash, showing the SUV turning into the community entrance as the teen crossed in front of it. The teen was thrown from the motorcycle, and the affidavit says the SUV backed up and drove away while he lay on the ground waving his arms. He was taken to Tradition Medical Center and then flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where police said he was treated for a broken left femur and an injured left ankle and listed in serious but stable condition. One witness told police the electric motorcycle had no headlights, and two witnesses said both vehicles were traveling fast. The SUV's owner, who is the father of Barthelemy's girlfriend, called 911 after Barthelemy told him he had hit someone on a bike and driven home. Officers found Barthelemy at his home on Southwest Ridgecrest Drive, where he told police he felt and heard the crash, knew immediately he had hit a person, and said he should have stopped but didn't. He said his phone was dead, according to the affidavit. Barthelemy is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving injuries, a felony, and was also given a traffic citation. He was released on a $7,500 bond.

The second case happened earlier that same day. According to an arrest affidavit, a Port St. Lucie officer clocked a silver Toyota going 85 mph in a 40-mph zone and tried to stop it. The driver went over a concrete median into oncoming lanes, ran a red light, and hit a traffic sign at Southwest Becker Road and Southwest Hallmark Street before getting onto northbound Interstate 95. The officer turned off his lights and siren but kept the car in sight as it later broke down on the shoulder of I-95. Police said the driver, Johnson, got out and ran toward the back of the car. A Port St. Lucie detective, a Florida Highway Patrol trooper, and the officer surrounded the vehicle, and Johnson was taken into custody. The affidavit says Johnson's license had been suspended three times. He is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, reckless driving, and driving with a suspended or revoked license, all misdemeanors. He was released on a $12,500 bond.

In a statement addressing both arrests, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said drivers are legally required to stop, whether for a traffic stop or after a crash. "Fleeing from law enforcement or leaving the scene of a crash can have serious consequences," the department said.

hero.headline: Indian River County Rabies Alert Follows Positive Bat Near Fellsmere Apartments
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments in Fellsmere tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in September.

Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population.

Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease.

Officials recommend several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure. These include keeping pets vaccinated against rabies, supervising pets and keeping them on a leash, securing livestock on private property, avoiding contact with wild or stray animals including cats, not feeding or handling wildlife, and preventing bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. More information on rabies is available through the Florida Department of Health website.

hero.headline: GreenMarket, Bahamian Festival and Oktoberfest Headline Treasure Coast Weekend
hero.body:
Treasure Coast residents have a full slate of events to choose from this weekend, including the 30th annual Bahamian Festival in Stuart and the first-ever Port St. Lucie Oktoberfest at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center. The West Palm Beach GreenMarket also opens its 32nd season Saturday, giving Treasure Coast visitors another option if they head south.

The 30th annual Bahamian Festival takes place Saturday at 11 a.m. at New Monrovia Park, 4453 SE Murray St. in Stuart. The festival invites families to celebrate the culture and traditions of the Bahamas with food, music, crafts and community connections.

Oktoberfest comes to the MIDFLORIDA Event Center, 9221 SE Event Center Place in Port St. Lucie, on Saturday starting at 5 p.m. The event features German music, Bavarian food, dancing and a wiener dog race.

For those willing to make the drive south, the West Palm Beach GreenMarket begins its 32nd season Saturday at 8 a.m. at 101 S. Clematis St. in West Palm Beach. The market will feature traditions from over 20 countries alongside its usual offerings. Other Palm Beach County events Saturday include the fourth annual Girls Rock concert at Tiki 52 Bar Grill from noon to 6 p.m., supporting the Sari Center for Integrative Cancer Care, the Norton Museum of Art's Nuestra Cultura Community Day at 1450 S. Dixie Highway starting at 11 a.m. with free admission and parking, and the West Palm Beach Antiques Festival at 9067 Southern Blvd. starting at 9 a.m., featuring hundreds of vendors at the South Florida Fairgrounds.

hero.headline: Missing Jensen Beach Man Nicklaus Cantor Found Safe
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office has confirmed that Nicklaus Tyre Cantor, a 29-year-old autistic man who went missing Thursday morning from his Jensen Beach residence, has been found safe. Deputies had been searching for Cantor since he was last seen around 8:50 a.m. and had asked the public for help locating him, but that search has now concluded with his safe recovery.

Cantor was reported missing after he was last seen at his home in Jensen Beach. The sheriff's office said he was believed to be traveling on foot and did not have a cell phone with him, which complicated efforts to track his whereabouts. Deputies described him as autistic and noted he may display childlike mannerisms, information they shared to help the public identify him if spotted.

Authorities released a physical description of Cantor to aid in the search, noting that he stands 5 feet 4 inches tall and weighs approximately 110 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes. The sheriff's office also said he is known to walk to a Walmart location in Port St. Lucie and may have had luggage with him at the time he went missing, details that were included in the public alert asking residents to watch for him.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office has not released additional information about where Cantor was found or the circumstances surrounding his safe recovery. The case adds to a string of recent missing persons matters in the region, including an ongoing search by a Port St. Lucie family for a father who has been missing for eight months with no resolution.

cards.headline: West Nile Virus Advisory Issued for Martin County After Chickens Test Positive
cards.teaser: Sentinel chickens in Martin County have tested positive for West Nile virus, prompting a health advisory and expanded mosquito control efforts.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health in Martin County is informing residents that several sentinel chickens have tested positive for West Nile virus. The department and Martin County Mosquito Control said they are coordinating surveillance and prevention efforts through enhanced monitoring for mosquitoes and disease, along with targeted mosquito treatment to reduce the risk of transmission.

The health department said individuals with symptoms of fever, chills, sweats, nausea or vomiting, and headache should seek immediate medical attention.

Residents are being reminded to avoid mosquito bites by eliminating standing water around their homes. The health department said mosquitoes breed by laying eggs in and near standing water, and as little as one bottle cap of water left standing for more than a week is enough for mosquitoes to multiply.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Attorney Gives 90-Day Notice Amid Hazing Dispute
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol submitted her 90-day resignation notice Wednesday as the district fights its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted the notice Wednesday and said her last work day will be December 31, 2026. She said her employment agreement, a three-year contract, requires 90 days' notice. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing labor dispute.

Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement that the District Attorney is eligible for retirement and that the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters," the agency said.

Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees.

Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp has said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. "There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp said. The union has challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV, with Sapp saying union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration.

Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie TikTok Creator Jailed Again as Computer Access Case Reopens
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie man who describes himself online as a cybersecurity engineer is back in the St. Lucie County Jail after police reopened an investigation into claims he accessed women's electronic devices and exposed their private information in TikTok videos. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. The case had been closed in May, and an earlier stalking charge against him appears to have been dropped.

The renewed charge stems from an investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women's devices and discussing information they said was private in posts on TikTok. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from a TikTok account linked to Asea, whose bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman's password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she never gave Asea permission to share it.

Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She told investigators she became concerned after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six videos in a single day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization.

Asea was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on the reopened charge, and his booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce's South Indian River Drive washes out for second time in a week
cards.teaser: Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to repair the same embankment they fixed days earlier, as king tides and rain keep eroding the roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon.
cards.body:
Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to repair a washed-out embankment for the second time in a week. King tides and recent rain continue to affect parts of South Florida, and the latest damage came only days after an earlier repair job on the same stretch of road. Skid loaders worked along the narrow roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon, adding dirt and sand to reinforce an area where erosion has left the road's edge vulnerable. Crews had already brought 32 loads of dirt to the site in September before the embankment needed repairs again.

Resident Gene Barnes said the recurring work is not a long-term solution. "We're losing ground year by year," Barnes said. "Until the Corps of Engineers or something like that comes and puts a headwall in to stabilize it, it's not going to be an easy fix."

The road has faced erosion problems before. Heavy rain damaged sections in 2014, and Hurricane Nicole caused additional washouts in 2022. Barnes warned that continued rain and tidal action could undermine the roadway itself. "If we keep getting rains like this, it's going to undermine the road, and then the road is going to collapse and the school bus is going to fall in the hole," he said.

The latest repairs follow an emergency sand operation at nearby Jetty Park that cost taxpayers nearly $500,000. Repairs on South Indian River Drive may cost less, but residents said the erosion is likely to remain a concern as more rain and tidal action are forecast.

cards.headline: Mimms' Niece Testifies on Nonprofit Lease Deal in Fort Pierce Trial
cards.teaser: The corruption trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Mimms continued with testimony from his niece and an FDLE investigator, and is expected to carry into next week.
cards.body:
The trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Mimms continued Thursday with testimony from his niece and a lead investigator in the case. Mimms faces accusations of bid tampering and official misconduct tied to a lease deal for two city-owned properties.

The prosecution's key witness was Caleta Scott, Mimms' niece and one of the founders of the nonprofit Lincoln Park Young Professionals. Mimms is accused of using his position as city manager to help the nonprofit secure the lease to develop the properties. The prosecution argues Scott received special treatment because of her relationship with Mimms and presented it as a conflict of interest.

"Mimms was my uncle when I applied," Scott said during her testimony. Asked about her relationship with Mimms, she said, "I respected him in the role of city manager and called him Mr. Mimms." The defense has previously argued that Mimms and Scott have a distant relationship and that Mimms did not conspire to commit the alleged crimes.

The first witness called to the stand Thursday was one of the lead investigators in the case, from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. Cross-examination of that investigator became tense at times. The trial in Fort Pierce is expected to continue into next week.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Attorney Resigns Amid Union Firing Fight
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol has submitted her 90-day notice to resign as the agency fights its firefighters' union over the firing of three employees in a bug-zapper hazing case. Her last day is set for Dec. 31, 2026.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol submitted her 90-day notice to resign Wednesday as the agency continues an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday and said her last work day will be Dec. 31, 2026. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute.

Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement that Sabol is eligible for retirement and that the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters," the statement said.

Sabol's departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees.

Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp has said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV, with Sapp saying union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office handles cases involving missing persons with autism and other vulnerable individuals as part of its regular duties, often relying on community tips to help locate those who have gone missing. Cantor's case followed that pattern, with deputies turning to the public for help before announcing he had been found.

cards.headline: Palm City hoarding case: 72 charges against O'Donnell, dogs find homes
cards.teaser: Paige O'Donnell's attorney says he just received discovery in the case involving 36 rescued border collies, as nearly all the dogs find adoptive homes ahead of a Dec. 1 hearing.
cards.body:
A criminal case against Paige O'Donnell, the Palm City woman accused in the hoarding of 36 border collies rescued from her Martin County home in August, is moving toward its next hearing on Dec. 1. O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges, two for each dog rescued, including an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for every dog. She has pleaded not guilty.

O'Donnell was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon at the Martin County courthouse. Her attorney, Russell Ferraro, said the defense only recently received discovery in the case. "We just got the discovery in the case yesterday," Ferraro said. "We're organizing it, going through it, and we'll take it from there." Ferraro declined to characterize the case for or against his client at this stage, saying, "At this point I can't really say anything on her behalf for or against her." He added, "Everybody's got a right to a fair trial and to due process."

It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies removed the 36 dogs from O'Donnell's feces-filled home in August. Martin County condemned the house days after the border collies were rescued. Ferraro said O'Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house undergoes repair.

While the criminal case continues, most of the rescued dogs have found new homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the 36 dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Among the adopters, Cale and Colleen Tilley near Deltona each took in one of the rescued border collies, now named Nadia and Leila. Tilley said Leila was frightened when she first arrived home in September, hiding under the bed rather than going near the front door, but has since warmed up. "Now she just runs straight through the sliding glass door, or into it," Tilley said. Cale said Nadia goes to work with him every day and typically warms up to new people once offered a treat. Both adopters said their dogs have been working through old habits, including jumping onto countertops, which Tilley speculated was tied to how the dogs previously got food. Tilley, who showed dogs with her family as a child, said she remembered O'Donnell's reputation for well-bred and well-trained dogs and said she has struggled to understand what happened. Cale said he had been grieving the loss of his previous border collie, Jessie, who died of cancer about a year before he learned about the dogs from Palm City. "You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog," Cale said.

hero.headline: Family Still Searching 8 Months After Fort Pierce Man Vanished
hero.body:
Eight months after Robert La Polla disappeared following his release from a hospital in Fort Pierce, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the pain of not knowing where he is. La Polla, 47, a Port St. Lucie father, vanished Jan. 8 and has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirms the case remains unsolved, with no confirmed sightings of La Polla.

"I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, La Polla's sister. Finley said her brother struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often.

"Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital.

"We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. "She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him."

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

cards.headline: FDLE Agent: Promised Lincoln Theater Parking Language Left Out of Fort Pierce RFP
cards.teaser: An FDLE agent testified Thursday in the bid-tampering trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms that a parking provision he promised for the Lincoln Theater never appeared in the RFP sent to the purchasing department.
cards.body:
Former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms is on trial over allegations he improperly influenced a city bidding process involving two vacant lots in Fort Pierce's Lincoln Park area. Mimms faces charges of bid tampering and official misconduct and has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors allege he steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals, a nonprofit whose board included Mimms' niece and another city employee.

Testimony Thursday focused on who controlled the RFP process and how closely Mimms remained involved after it was handed over to the city's purchasing department. FDLE Agent Derek Brisky testified about emails and other records collected during the investigation, including communications tied to the nearby Lincoln Theater and its need for parking. Brisky also testified investigators found no evidence Mimms filed a 2019 memorandum concerning the parking plans in relevant city records.

The defense questioned the significance of that omission and emphasized that the purchasing department was responsible for putting together and publishing the RFP after receiving the project's specifications. Defense attorneys also challenged the state's characterization of the process as a sole-source arrangement, and Brisky acknowledged the RFP was not technically a sole-source contract. The state pointed to emails showing Mimms continued to communicate with city employees about the RFP, including its evaluation criteria and the evaluation committee. Other emails showed city employees knew there had been one submission after the RFP was posted, and an LPYP email address was copied on one of those communications. The defense also questioned the investigation's treatment of other city employees involved in the process, including a purchasing official who was not charged.

Former Fort Pierce employee Kalita Scott also testified Thursday about Lincoln Park Young Professionals and its efforts to develop the Lincoln Park properties. She described the organization as a group of young professionals focused on community development and said the need for parking near the Lincoln Theater was known in the community. Prosecutors allege Mimms manipulated the city's process to ensure LPYP received the lease. The defense has argued Mimms did not improperly favor the organization and that the evidence does not establish a criminal conspiracy. The trial is continuing in St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Video Shows SUV Rollover on Florida's Turnpike Ramp Near Bayshore Blvd
cards.teaser: Dashcam footage captured an SUV losing control and flipping over on a Turnpike ramp near Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie Thursday morning.
cards.body:
An SUV lost control on a Florida's Turnpike ramp near Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie Thursday morning, crossed into oncoming traffic and overturned, according to video posted by the SLC Scanner Facebook page. The dashboard-camera footage, recorded shortly after 8 a.m., shows the SUV traveling around a curve on the ramp before it appears to lose control, swerve across the center line into the opposite lane and flip over as other vehicles travel nearby.

A community-news page operated by Dan Toback reported that a witness called 911 after seeing dangerous driving near the Turnpike entrance. The page reported the SUV had been traveling at a high speed and that drivers behind it had to stop.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol Gives 90-Day Notice
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney Kim Sabol submitted her resignation notice as the agency fights its firefighters' union over the discipline of five employees accused of hazing rookies with a modified bug zapper.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District attorney Kim Sabol submitted a 90-day notice of resignation Wednesday, with her last work day set for Dec. 31, 2026. Her departure comes as the district faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the discipline of five employees, three of whom were terminated and accused of hazing rookies.

Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. She confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday but it was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement that the attorney is eligible for retirement and that the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters," the statement said.

Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees.

Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp has said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV, with Sapp saying union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union has raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration, and two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation.

Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man gets probation for hiding gun in June shooting, no charges yet for shooter
cards.teaser: Christopher Williams Jr. pleaded no contest to hiding the firearm used in a June shooting that wounded a 17-year-old girl on North 19th Street. The man accused of pulling the trigger has not been charged.
cards.body:
Christopher Williams Jr., 19, of Fort Pierce, has been sentenced to six months of probation after pleading no contest to charges stemming from a June shooting that wounded a 17-year-old girl on the 500 block of North 19th Street. Williams Jr. entered the plea on Sept. 3 to charges of false statement to law enforcement and tampering with evidence, according to court documents in St. Lucie County. As part of the plea agreement with the State Attorney's Office, he was also ordered to pay court costs. He had faced a maximum penalty of six years in a state prison and a $6,000 fine.

The shooting happened June 2. Williams Jr. initially told Fort Pierce Police Department officers that he was inside his home during the shooting and was not aware it had happened. A witness told officers that Williams Jr. was given the gun after 18-year-old Ja'Shawn Crosby shot his 17-year-old girlfriend following an altercation. In a second interview with police, Williams Jr. admitted he hid the firearm on the property before Crosby left the scene.

Despite the witness account and Williams Jr.'s admission that he hid the weapon used in the shooting, Crosby has not been charged in the case. The State Attorney's Office announced on July 8 that it would not pursue an attempted second-degree murder charge against Crosby, citing insufficient evidence to prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt.

The resolution of Williams Jr.'s case closes out the charges against the man accused of concealing the weapon, while the shooting that wounded the 17-year-old girl remains without anyone charged as the shooter. Williams Jr.'s six months of probation stands as the only criminal consequence issued so far in connection with the June 2 shooting on North 19th Street.

cards.headline: Port Salerno Toddler's Pond Drowning Ruled Accidental by Medical Examiner
cards.teaser: The Martin County Medical Examiner has ruled the death of 23-month-old Pablo Mendoza-Arrojo an accidental drowning after he was found unresponsive in a pond on his family's Port Salerno property. Sheriff John Budensiek and YMCA Treasure Coast leadership are urging families to take steps to protect children around water.
cards.body:
The Martin County Medical Examiner has officially ruled the drowning death of 23-month-old Pablo Mendoza-Arrojo an accidental drowning. The toddler was found unresponsive in a pond on his family's property near Southeast Darling Street and Southeast Taylor Drive in Port Salerno. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the child's parents called 911 to report the emergency. "We received one of the most heart wrenching 911 calls you can get," Budensiek said.

According to investigators, Pablo was outside in the yard with family members shortly after 5 p.m. when he slipped out of sight for a short time. When his mother and aunt realized he was missing, they began a frantic search and found him in the pond. Family members told investigators Pablo had been out of sight for no more than 10 minutes. The family rushed him to Cleveland Clinic South, where despite lifesaving efforts he was pronounced dead in the emergency room.

Budensiek said a fence had once surrounded the pond but had been trampled down or broken over time, leaving it not functional. Martin County Sheriff's Office criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene, and the sheriff said it does not appear that anyone acted recklessly. "Parents get distracted, I know that," Budensiek said. "So, no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning. But we have to remember where we live and take the time and the effort or spend the money. Whatever you have to do to try to drown proof your child," Budensiek said.

Charlene Lyons, President and CEO of YMCA Treasure Coast, said she was devastated when she heard the news. "I started at the 'Y' as a lifeguard, so aquatic safety is paramount to me," Lyons said. She encouraged families to contact the YMCA for information about swim lessons. "Drowning is the great equalizer — it goes across every demographic, socioeconomic status — it doesn't matter, so it's important for everyone to learn to swim," Lyons said. The family has set up a GoFundMe account to help during this difficult time, and information about swim lessons is available through the YMCA Treasure Coast website.
